cards.lore: The institution doesn't love you back. It just manages you as a resource.
cards.power: Discard a player's loyalty token to save yourself.

cards.lore: Treason doesn't wear a mask; a cheap suit and denies your pension.
cards.power: Stall the game for 3 turns. Nobody gets to play.

cards.lore: The apparatus always sacrifices its agents. The only question is when.
cards.power: Force the player with the most points to lose half.

cards.lore: Espionage is 90% filing reports about lies you told to other liars.
cards.power: Reveal a hidden objective card.

cards.lore: Too many missions, too many names. He runs out, but the door is walled over.
cards.power: Ignore one attack, but you cannot draw cards next turn due to sheer apathy.

cards.lore: Naïve idealism is the most dangerous form of espionage.
cards.power: Gain +2 strength, but auto-lose if a 'Truth' card is played.

cards.lore: He changed sides. Now nobody believes his story, least of all himself.
cards.power: Swap hands with an opponent, inheriting all their penalties.

cards.lore: The realization of sacrifice isn't a scream. It's absolute, hollow silence.
cards.power: Silence a player for one round.

cards.lore: Live the role long enough, and the original identity dissolves entirely.
cards.power: Copy another card's ability permanently, but discard your original name.

cards.lore: What remains of a person after they've been used as a tool for a decade?
cards.power: Nullify an opponent's disguise.

cards.lore: At some point, the fake loyalty becomes the only real thing left.
cards.power: Force an opponent to play their next 3 turns with cards facing outward.

cards.lore: Identity erosion isn't a side effect; it is the core mechanic of the system.
cards.power: Play two conflicting action cards at once; take 2 damage to your own psyche.

cards.lore: Technology cannot replace psychology. Gadgets just make the body bags heavier.
cards.power: Destroy an enemy card, but lose 2 health from the inevitable shrapnel.

cards.lore: Glamour is a fantasy projection to hide the institutional trauma.
cards.power: Look flashy, do exactly zero damage.

cards.lore: A spy who makes no mistakes isn't a spy. It's boring corporate slop.
cards.power: Cancel a damage effect, but discard your entire hand in embarrassment.

cards.lore: "Patriot" isn't a character motivation; it's the lie they feed you at the door.
cards.power: Steal an opponent's turn by shouting "For the Country!"

cards.lore: Every information could be false. Every figure. Paranoia isn't a stylistic device. It is the baseline epistemic reality.
cards.power: Redirect an attack to a random third party.
Rebound any Lore effect back at the caster.

cards.lore: The audience no longer knows who to trust. The spy forgot years ago.
cards.power: Everyone must suddenly shuffle their active hands into the draw deck.

cards.lore: Trust is just a currency waiting to be shorted.
cards.power: Peek at a card. If it's a Trap, you instantly lose.

cards.lore: Spies never speak directly. The real information hides in the pauses and polite smiles.
cards.power: Force an opponent to discard a card of their choice via intense politeness.

cards.lore: A conversation where both know the other is lying, but courtesy demands silence. Politeness as a threat.
cards.power: Play a card face down; it triggers three turns from now.

cards.lore: Two bosses, two different directives for the same op. Navigate the verbal minefield.
cards.power: Give two opponents completely contradictory rules for the next turn.

cards.lore: True tradecraft is found in false self-corrections and strategic topic changes.
cards.power: Skip the current phase entirely.

cards.lore: It starts with a minor compromise. Just a look away. Just one uncomfortable task.
cards.power: Steal exactly 1 resource from the poorest player.
Destroy a friendly card to gain an immediate advantage.

cards.lore: You don't leap into moral bankruptcy. You slide into it, one ignored atrocity at a time.
cards.power: Ignore a blatant rule violation this turn.

cards.lore: Only when you look back do you see the full, horrifying trajectory of your compromises.
cards.power: Take control of the game board.

cards.lore: Character A knows X and acts like they don't. That's the engine of the genre.
cards.power: Secretly leave a card under the table for someone else to find.

cards.lore: Character B knows Y and refuses to share it. Trust is just bad math.
cards.power: Hide your hand from all players for the rest of the game.

cards.lore: The audience knows more than the spy. It's a tragedy disguised as a thriller.
cards.power: Reveal a secret rule only you and one other player know.

cards.lore: Secrets aren't facts; they are leverage.
cards.power: Gain points for every card your opponents haven't played yet.

cards.lore: Modern espionage tells the exact same story, just in server rooms instead of embassy parks.
cards.power: Look at the top 3 cards of the deck and rearrange them.

cards.lore: Knows the truth, speaks it, and pays the ultimate price. The public vs. The Apparatus.
cards.power: Reveal everyone's hidden cards; you lose your next turn and go into exile.

cards.lore: You aren't a person anymore. You are a profile, perfectly predicted.
cards.power: Count the cards in an opponent's discard pile to perfectly guess their next move.

cards.lore: Cold, precise, democratic tracking. Anyone can be a spy. Everyone is a target.
cards.power: Force a player to repeat their exact last action.

cards.lore: LORE (Courier Prime): Espionage exacts a physical toll. You can't outrun the exhaustion of the body.
cards.power: POWER (Courier Prime): Drop a card randomly from your hand onto the table.

cards.lore: LORE (Courier Prime): The ultimate reward for a lifetime of service: dying completely alone.
cards.power: POWER (Courier Prime): You cannot be targeted, but you also cannot attack or interact.

cards.lore: LORE (Courier Prime): Memory failure isn't a glitch; it's the brain trying to protect itself from the lies.
cards.power: POWER (Courier Prime): Blank out the text of one opponent's card, making it useless.

cards.lore: LORE (Courier Prime): The heart doesn't break; it just stops feeling anything at all to survive the frost.
cards.power: POWER (Courier Prime): Ignore all Lore effects for one round.

cards.lore: Loyalty to the machine vs. the desperate urge to survive. The machine usually wins.
cards.power: Choose between losing your entire hand or losing half your health.

cards.lore: What are you really fighting for, and what happens when you realize the cause is rotten?
cards.power: Discard a 'Good' alignment card to forcefully play an 'Evil' action.

cards.lore: In an emergency, loyalty is the first thing jettisoned. Who sacrifices whom first?
cards.power: Sacrifice a teammate's card to block a lethal attack aimed at you.

cards.lore: To whom do you owe your loyalty when every single side is covered in filth?
cards.power: End the game immediately in a deeply unsatisfying draw.

cards.lore: LORE (Courier Prime): You can't beat the system. You can only decide how it crushes you.
cards.power: POWER (Courier Prime): Predict the exact turn you will lose. If correct, you steal the win.

cards.lore: LORE (Courier Prime): The aesthetic of doom. Action meets Detective meets existential despair.
cards.power: POWER (Courier Prime): Obscure the board; no one can read card texts for one full turn.

cards.lore: LORE (Courier Prime): Ethics under extreme conditions. There is no clean way out of the shadows.
cards.power: POWER (Courier Prime): Take severe damage to deal double damage to an opponent.

cards.lore: LORE (Courier Prime): Betrayal isn't a twist; it's the perfectly logical consequence of the game.
cards.power: POWER (Courier Prime): Lock one enemy card permanently. It cannot be moved or played.

cards.lore: Espionage is just an extreme mirror of our platform-driven, self-surveilled reality.
cards.power: Broadcast your hand face-up to the table for +1 resource per turn.

cards.lore: Cognitive warfare and over-shared privacy. We built our own panopticon.
cards.power: Change the core rules of the game for one round.

cards.lore: Information is no longer just power. It is the only currency that matters.
cards.power: Sell an opponent's secret objective to the highest bidder.

cards.lore: There is no 'private' self left. Just a string of exploitable data points.
cards.power: Auto-counter an opponent based solely on their previous plays.

cards.lore: LORE (Courier Prime): Deconstruct trust completely. Break the fourth wall and burn the pieces.
cards.power: POWER (Courier Prime): Rip a dummy card in half (literally) to destroy two targets simultaneously.

cards.lore: LORE (Courier Prime): When the system is rigged, the only valid strategy is absolute Dadaist anarchy.
cards.power: POWER (Courier Prime): Physically place this card over another to combine their texts.

cards.lore: LORE (Courier Prime): The truth is a joke, so you might as well be the one holding the punchline.
cards.power: POWER (Courier Prime): Ignore all rules. Draw a picture on the table. If people laugh, you survive.

cards.lore: LORE (Courier Prime): We're all just animals playing a rigged game of epistemic collapse. Stay fluffy!
cards.power: POWER (Courier Prime): Win instantly if you can convince the table of a blatant, hilarious lie.
